text:
Support Ops: FYI customer AcmeApp opened a support ticket — lots of 500s from our hosted inference API (not 429s). They started seeing it around 08:12 PDT, high request rate but previously they received 429s. Customer says this affects prod latency and UX. Attaching short logs they pasted below.

sre-bot: alert: quota-gateway error-rate increase -> 5xx spike (08:13). Pager triggered to oncall team.

Alex K: assigning to this thread — I'm oncall, looking.

Maria G: customer sample cURL they sent:

```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" -d '{"model":"gpt-4-small","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
{"error":"rate service failed","request_id":"r-0a1b2c3d"}
```

Jordan L: I see similar 500s in our ingress logs for that request_id r-0a1b2c3d. Upstream to quota-orchestrator returned 504/timeout on several calls and then the gateway returned 500 back to client.

Maria G: pulled quota-orch logs around t=08:12-08:18: lots of gRPC timeouts to token-store and classifier service. Example:

```
[08:12:14] quota-orch: rpc call token-store.LookupTokens ctx deadline exceeded
[08:12:14] quota-orch: fallback classify -> ERROR
[08:12:14] quota-orch: returning status INTERNAL (500) to gateway
```

Anshul R: hunch — if token-store times out, quota-orch goes down a fallback code path that currently maps failures to 500 rather than returning a 4xx for rate-limit. That would explain why customers see 500s instead of 429s. Need to confirm where the mapping occurs (classifier vs. gateway) and whether a timeout should be a 503/504 rather than 500.

Ted (oncall): definitely customer-facing impact. Quick mitigation: can we flip gateway to treat quota-orch INTERNAL or timeout as "rate-limited" (429) for short term? Or add a conservative bypass for customers with prod keys so they don't all get 500s.

Alex K: exploring quick mitigations. Two ideas:
- short-term: gateway mapping rule change (config) to translate quota-orch INTERNAL/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED -> 429 for a 30m window
- medium-term: patch quota-orch to: increase token-store deadline, classify timeout -> 429, and emit richer metrics

deploy-bot: found an existing feature flag `gateway.quota_fallback_to_429` (dev flag) — not enabled in prod. Could toggle to true in prod region us-west-2 for 30m canary.

Jordan L: repro steps I ran locally (stressor):
```
# simulate token-store slow
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"model":"gpt-4-small"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
```
I see 5xx starting when token-store CPU maxes and gRPC calls hit deadline.

Maria G: metrics snapshot:
- quota-orch p95 latency jumped 30ms -> 2100ms
- token-store CPU 96% for ~3m
- gRPC deadline_exceeded spikes correlate with 5xx window

Anshul R: root cause hypothesis: a transient token-store stall (GC / backup job?) caused gRPC deadlines; quota-orch's fallback mapping incorrectly returns INTERNAL/500 rather than 429/503. Because our customer-facing gateway has no special mapping for this specific error code, client sees a 500. That matches customer reports that they used to see 429s and now see 500s.

Ted (oncall): action plan
1) Immediate (10-30m): enable feature flag `gateway.quota_fallback_to_429=true` in us-west-2 for all routes -> reduces customer-visible 500s. (owner: Alex)
2) Short-term (1-3h): patch quota-orch to treat token-store deadline_exceeded as rate-deny vs internal error; add logging/metric. (owner: Anshul)
3) Medium-term (24-72h): add circuit-breaker and increase token-store replica counts / tune GC. (owner: Maria)
4) Customer comms: support to notify AcmeApp and offer credits + ETA. (owner: Support Ops)

Alex K: toggled flag in us-west-2 canary at 08:24 (10% traffic). Observed error-rate drop of 5xx -> 429 on canary. Deploy-bot: canary -> 100% rollout at 08:34.

deploy-bot: PR merged: r/orch#452 - map DEADLINE_EXCEEDED->RATE_LIMIT (internal change), rollout planned.

Anshul R: pushed hotfix to quota-orch (branch fix/token-timeout-map). Patch does two things:
- map token-store deadline_exceeded and classifier timeouts to `RATE_DENIED` result -> gateway will return 429
- extend token-store RPC timeout from 200ms -> 500ms and add a histogram metric for rpc latency

deploy-bot: hotfix deployed to canary 08:46 -> 100% prod at 09:02. No rollback required.

Maria G: after patch metrics stabilized: token-store CPU normalized (we autoscaled one extra replica), quota-orch p95 back to ~45ms, client 5xx rate dropped to baseline and replaced by 429s for throttled flows. Confirmed with AcmeApp sample requests — they now get 429s instead of 500s.

Support Ops: messaged AcmeApp at 09:20: apology + explanation + credits offer. They confirmed reduced failure rate and accepted credits. Customer asked for postmortem.

Alex K: quick postmortem notes for later:
- Trigger: token-store stall during backup/GC led to gRPC timeouts
- Weakness: quota-orch fallback mapping treated transient timeouts as internal errors (500)
- Impact: several customers saw 500s instead of expected 429s; degraded UX and support load
- Fixes: feature-flag mitigation + quota-orch mapping fix + increased token-store resilience

Ted (oncall): leaving action items
- Anshul: follow-up PR to add unit tests for error mapping + add synthetic test harness (ETA 2d)
- Maria: confirm token-store GC schedule and add runbook to scale before backup (ETA 3d)
- Alex: draft postmortem and customer-facing summary (ETA 1d)
- Support Ops: finalize credits and close ticket (ETA 4h)

support-bot: ticket #C-3421 updated -> status: customer-verified, awaiting postmortem.

Alex K: closing thread for now, will post final postmortem link when ready. Thanks all for quick triage. :thumbsup:
